raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

A pre-tokenized `/v1/completions` `prompt` can contain token ids in `[tokenizer_vocab, model_vocab)`. The model can embed those ids, but the Rust frontend also uses prompt ids as left context for streaming detokenization. If the tokenizer cannot map one prompt id back to token text, `DecodeStream` prefix seeding fails the stream with a tokenizer error before generation can continue.

This keeps `Tokenizer::decode` strict and limits the tolerance to prompt-context seeding in `DecodeStream`. Prompt context first tries the normal decode; if that fails, it retries with only prompt ids that `id_to_token` can resolve. Generated ids still use the regular decode path, so this PR does not add generated-token filtering.

## Test Plan

- A table-driven Rust tokenizer test for prompt-context filtering and generated-token strictness.
- End-to-end Rust frontend streaming comparison on `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with one normal prompt and one pre-tokenized prompt id in `[len(tokenizer), model_vocab)`.
- Rust workspace formatting, clippy, and tests.

## Test Result

E2E used an RTX 4090 and local model files for `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (`len(tokenizer)=151669`, `config.vocab_size=151936`). The probe id was `151669`, which is below the model vocabulary but cannot be decoded by the tokenizer.

| request | baseline Rust frontend | this PR | health after probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| prompt `"Hi"` | streamed normal completion | streamed normal completion | 200 |
| prompt `[151669]` | streamed `server_error`: `unknown token ID: 151669` | streamed normal completion | 200 |

<details>
<summary>E2E command and output</summary>

Server command:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=/root/autodl-tmp/bin/vllm-rs-44682-fixed \
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
/root/autodl-tmp/conda_envs/vllm/bin/vllm serve /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --port 8762 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \
  --max-model-len 512
```

Probe:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8762/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B","prompt":[151669],"max_tokens":1,"stream":true}'
```

Baseline output:

```text
data: {"error":{"message":"tokenizer error: decoding failed: unknown token ID: 151669","type":"server_error","code":"server_error"}}

data: [DONE]
```

This PR:

```text
data: {"id":"cmpl-07696faf","object":"text_completion","created":1782853758,"model":"/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"ED"}]}

data: {"id":"cmpl-07696faf","object":"text_completion","created":1782853758,"model":"/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"","finish_reason":"length"}]}

data: [DONE]
```

</details>

Other checks:

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo test -p vllm-tokenizer
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --exclude vllm-chat
```

`cargo test --workspace` still cannot complete `vllm-chat --test roundtrip` on this machine because those tests fetch external Hugging Face model files; direct HF timed out and `hf-mirror.com` returned missing `content-range` for several tokenizer config downloads.

AI assistance was used to prepare this PR.

cc @BugenZhao

nodes.body:
Hi @BugenZhao #44680 bounds completion `prompt_token_ids` by `max(tokenizer_vocab, model_vocab)`, so a pre-tokenized prompt id in `[tokenizer_vocab, model_vocab)` still passes validation and then 500s in the Rust detokenizer when it seeds the prefix (the tokenizer's `id_to_token` returns `None`). This PR closes that gap by skipping such ids on decode, matching the Python tokenizer, so the two frontends agree on every id.

Did this one just slip the queue, or do you have a different plan for that range (reject those ids too, or handle it elsewhere)?

> Hi @BugenZhao #44680 bounds completion `prompt_token_ids` by `max(tokenizer_vocab, model_vocab)`, so a pre-tokenized prompt id in `[tokenizer_vocab, model_vocab)` still passes validation and then 500s in the Rust detokenizer when it seeds the prefix (the tokenizer's `id_to_token` returns `None`). This PR closes that gap by skipping such ids on decode, matching the Python tokenizer, so the two frontends agree on every id.
> 
> Did this one just slip the queue, or do you have a different plan for that range (reject those ids too, or handle it elsewhere)?

Thanks. I think the motivation for this PR makes sense. I just feel that it might not be the right place to add the tolerance in the HF tokenizer impl:

- this behavior should be agnostic to any tokenizer
- not all callers would expect tolerance here, so it would be better to handle this in the actual place where we need it, such as the initialization of the incremental detokenizer.

Thanks @BugenZhao, I reworked this along the direction you suggested: the diff is now limited to `DecodeStream` prompt-context seeding, `Tokenizer::decode` and generated-token unknown ids stay strict, and the `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` prompt `[151669]` E2E now completes normally.

If this still is not the direction you want, could you take over the remaining fix, either by pushing to this branch or opening a replacement PR?

Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use report formatting for tokenizer errors**

The `/workspace/vllm/rust/AGENTS.md` error-handling rule for this tree says not to call `to_string()` directly on error values and to use `ToReportString` or `AsReport` instead. This new assertion inspects a `TokenizerError` via `error.to_string()`, so it violates the required Rust convention for error message checks in this crate; use the report-formatting helper instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Thanks! This direction looks good to me. I've pushed a commit to adopt the newly introduced `TestTokenizer` (#47125) for testing
